note.note:
Consult Summary:
- Middle-aged man with ~4–5 days of viral-type upper respiratory symptoms (dry cough +/- small amount sputum, rhinorrhea, sore throat), subjective fever/chills and mild shortness of breath; clinician impression viral illness/possible early influenza with plan for supportive care and a delayed antibiotic prescription (amoxicillin) if not improving.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Feeling generally unwell for several days with cough, "cold" symptoms and feeling run-down.
- Onset, duration, progression:
  - Symptoms began approximately 4–5 days ago (patient states onset Saturday; consult on Wednesday).
  - Patient reports symptoms ongoing without resolution; some early diarrheal symptoms on the first day that have since resolved.
- Cough:
  - Mostly dry cough, worse in the morning.
  - Patient admits a small amount of sputum ("a wee bit mucky/firm") but predominantly dry.
- Upper airway symptoms:
  - Runny nose / sniffling noted by clinician over phone.
  - Sore throat; patient has not inspected throat carefully and did not note erythema or exudates.
- Breathing / chest:
  - Patient reports increased shortness of breath compared with baseline (patient and doctor statements conflict initially: clinician asked if breathing was fine, patient then stated "No... it's not good" and later confirmed some shortness of breath). No chest pain.
- Constitutional:
  - Subjective feverishness, night sweats / feeling hot and cold; patient has not measured temperature.
  - Myalgias/stiffness: generalized stiffness noted (elbows/knees) when bending/moving.
  - Appetite: reasonable; patient trying to keep fluids up.
- Gastrointestinal:
  - Brief diarrhoea on first day only; resolved; no ongoing nausea or vomiting.
- Review of systems / pertinent negatives mentioned:
  - No documented measured fever.
  - No chest pain.
  - No ongoing vomiting.
  - No formal ear pain, though patient reports some baseline decreased hearing; no new ear severe pain described.

Past Medical History:
- Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
  - No further details on duration, control, complications provided.
  - Medication: Metformin — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Hypertension (elevated blood pressure noted previously).
  - Medication: Lisinopril — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Occasional use of aspirin (intermittent) reported — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- No known drug allergies per patient (“not that I’m aware of; doctor never said”).

Social History:
- Lives with wife; children have left home.
- Employed in a local factory manufacturing steel parts.
- Alcohol: drinks approximately nine pints per week (patient estimate: ~4 pints Saturday, additional drinking across weekend).
- Smoking/tobacco/vaping:
  - Occasional cigarette use; currently using an electronic vaporizer and trying to cut down.
- No other substance use mentioned.
- No financial or other lifestyle constraints reported.

Family History:
- No family history provided or discussed in the transcript.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: none documented.
- Examination findings:
  - No formal physical exam documented.
  - Clinician noted audible sniffles on phone.
  - Patient reports he shaves daily and has looked at himself but has not specifically inspected pharynx for redness or white spots.
  - No documented lung auscultation, oxygen saturation, throat inspection, or other exam findings.

Investigations:
- None performed or reported during this consult.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute viral upper respiratory infection / possible early influenza
  - Assessment:
    - Clinical impression: likely viral respiratory illness, possible early influenza based on history of feverishness, myalgias, sore throat, rhinorrhea, and dry cough.
  - Plan:
    - Supportive care: rest and increased fluid intake recommended.
    - Antipyretic/analgesic: regular Paracetamol recommended for feeling hot/sweaty; dose/route/frequency not documented.
    - Delayed antibiotic strategy: clinician offered a prescription for Amoxicillin to be started if symptoms do not improve in 24–48 hours; prescription details discussed as "one tablet three times a day." Strength of tablet and route not documented.
    - Follow-up: re-assess if still unwell after one week.
- Issue 2: Shortness of breath (subjective, mild)
  - Assessment:
    - Patient reports increased breathlessness compared with baseline; not associated with chest pain; clinician concerned but did not diagnose pneumonia at this time.
    - Conflict in transcript regarding whether breathing was initially described as "fine" vs later "not good" (see Quality checks).
  - Plan:
    - Monitor symptoms at home.
    - If patient remains breathless and run-down in 24–48 hours, clinician advised starting the prescribed antibiotic (Amoxicillin 1 tablet three times daily; strength/route not documented).
    - Return for review if symptoms persist or worsen; if severe new breathlessness occurs, patient advised to seek urgent evaluation (note: urgent instructions for severe symptoms were not explicitly documented in the transcript beyond arranging follow-up).
- Issue 3: Chronic conditions — Type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension
  - Assessment:
    - Patient lists Metformin and Lisinopril as current medications; no acute changes recommended during this consult.
  - Plan:
    - Continue current prescribed medications as previously; no adjustments documented.
    - No additional chronic disease management actions documented in this encounter.
- General plan items:
  - Provide delayed prescription for antibiotics (Amoxicillin as above) to start if no improvement after 24–48 hours.
  - Return to clinic for review if not improved by one week.
  - Supportive measures: rest, hydration, paracetamol as needed.

document_quality / Quality checks:
- Missing but expected clinical elements:
  - No recorded vital signs (temperature, heart rate, respiratory rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation).
  - No physical examination of throat, lungs, heart, or full systemic exam documented.
  - No laboratory tests, chest X-ray or other investigations performed or documented.
  - Medication doses, routes, and frequencies not documented for Metformin, Lisinopril, and aspirin (patient provided names only).
  - Amoxicillin strength and route not documented (patient told "one tablet three times a day"; tablet strength not specified).
  - No objective measurement of fever despite subjective feverishness.
- Internal conflicts from the transcript:
  - Conflicting statements regarding breathing: clinician first asked if breathing was fine; patient responded inconsistently, at one point saying breathing was "not good" after earlier statements implying breathing was not labored. Conflict noted.
- Transcript quality comment:
  - Audio transcription largely intelligible; occasional conversational fillers and side comments (football discussion) present but clinical content identifiable. Some brief interruptions and colloquial language; no major sections inaudible.
